item.title: 1974: Catfish Hunter Wins His Only AL Cy Young Award
item.description: Catfish Hunter of the World Series champion Oakland Athletics (41 games started, 318 innings pitched, 25–12 win–loss record, 2.49 earned run average, 23 complete games, six shutouts) wins his only American League Cy Young Award. Photo: Doug McWilliams (Public domain).

item.title: 2025: SoftBank Hawks Beat Tigers, Win 12th Japan Series Title
item.description: The Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks defeat the Hanshin Tigers in game 5 of the 2025 Japan Series to win their 12th championship.

item.title: 2024: Dodgers Beat Yankees 4-1, Win Eighth World Series Title
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers defeat the New York Yankees 4–1, winning their eighth World Series championship in franchise history. Photo: Spanneraol (CC BY-SA 4.0).

item.title: 2024: Dodgers Erase 5-0 Deficit, Beat Yankees 7-6 in Game 5
item.description: On October 30, 2024, the Los Angeles Dodgers became the first visiting team to win a World Series at the venue when they erased a 5–0 deficit to defeat the Yankees 7–6 in Game 5 of the 2024 World Series.

item.title: 2020: Hinch Named Tigers Manager on Multi-Year Contract
item.description: On October 30, 2020, Hinch was named the manager of the Tigers, agreeing on a multi-year contract. Photo: EricEnfermero (CC BY-SA 4.0).

item.title: 2020: Indians Won't Bring Back Mills as Bench Coach for 2021
item.description: The Indians subsequently announced on October 30, 2020 that Mills will not return as bench coach for the 2021 season, but would remain with the club in an undetermined role. Photo: EricEnfermero (CC BY-SA 4.0).

item.title: 2019: Nationals Beat Astros 6-2, Win First World Series
item.description: The Washington Nationals win their first World Series in franchise history by defeating the Houston Astros 6–2 in game 7 of the World Series. Washington Nationals pitcher Stephen Strasburg was named 2019 World Series MVP. Photo: All-Pro Reels from District of Columbia, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2018: Ground Broken on New Downtown Kannapolis Ballpark
item.description: On October 30, 2018, ground was broken on a new ballpark in downtown Kannapolis as part of a mixed-use redevelopment plan.

item.title: 2018: Bill Fischer, 88, Longtime Pitcher and Pitching Coach
item.description: Bill Fischer, 88, who spent 71 years in baseball as a pitcher and pitching coach, including pitching for six clubs in a span of nine seasons from 1956 to 1964; coaching for the Reds (1979–1983), Red Sox (1985–1991) and Devil Rays (2000–2001); coaching and managing in the Braves minor league system (2002–2006); working as the Royals' senior pitching adviser (2007–2010) and pitching coordinator (2011–2018), winning a… Photo: Minda Haas Kuhlmann: flickr, personal website, twitter, instagram (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2015: Mets Rally Past Royals 9-3 in First Citi Field Series Game
item.description: The New York Mets rallied from an early deficit to beat the Kansas City Royals, 9–3, in the first World Series game ever played at Citi Field, which set a record when 44,781 fans attended the game. Noah Syndergaard settled down after yielding three runs and six hits in the first two innings, Curtis Granderson and David Wright each belted a two-run home run, as the Mets took Game 3 of the series after two tough… Photo: slgckgc (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2015: Mondesí Makes World Series Debut With Royals
item.description: Mondesí is the first player in modern MLB history to make his debut in the World Series, doing so with the Royals in Game 3 on October 30, 2015, against the New York Mets. Photo: Arturo Pardavila III on Flickr (Original version) UCinternational (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2013: Red Sox Beat Cardinals 6-1, Win Third Title in 10 Years
item.description: The Boston Red Sox defeat the St. Louis Cardinals 6–1 at Fenway Park and win their eighth World Series title and third in the last 10 seasons, to become the first team to win three world championship titles in the 21st century. Red Sox icon David Ortiz earns MVP honors. Photo: Rick Berry (Public domain).

item.title: 2011: MLB All-Stars Arrive in Taipei for Taiwan Series
item.description: MLB All-Stars arrive in Taipei for the beginning of the 2011 Taiwan All-Star Series. With Bruce Bochy at the helm, the American team includes players such as Robinson Canó, Curtis Granderson, Jeremy Guthrie, LaTroy Hawkins, Logan Morrison, Josh Reddick and Pablo Sandoval. Photo: Gage Skidmore (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 2011: Mickey Scott, 64, German-Born Reliever for Orioles, Expos
item.description: Mickey Scott, 64, German-born reliever for the Baltimore Orioles, Montreal Expos and California Angels between 1972 and 1977, who also was elected to the Rochester Red Wings Hall of Fame in 1998.

item.title: 2007: Sveum Switches Staff Positions, Becomes Third Base Coach
item.description: On October 30, 2007, Sveum switched positions on the staff and became the team's third base coach. Photo: thotfulspot (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2007: Yankees Sign Joe Girardi to Three-Year Managerial Deal
item.description: The Yankees sign Joe Girardi to a three-year deal as their new manager. In the meantime, amid rumors that Torre will be hired as the team's new manager, Grady Little resigns as manager of the Los Angeles Dodgers. Photo: Girardi in 2020 (CC BY 3.0).

item.title: 2005: Al López, 97, Hall of Fame Catcher and Manager
item.description: Al López, 97, Hall of Famer who set a major league record for career games as a catcher (1,918) in 1928 and from 1930 to 1947, almost entirely in the NL; then managed the Cleveland Indians (1951–1956) and Chicago White Sox (1957–1965, 1968–1969) to AL pennants in 1954 and 1959 — the only non-Yankee AL champs between 1949 and 1964. Photo: Jam Handy Organization (Public Domain).

item.title: 2001: Bush Throws Ceremonial First Pitch as Series Visits Yankee Stadium
item.description: The World Series comes to Yankee Stadium. President George W. Bush throws out the ceremonial first pitch. Photo: TLK in 3 (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 1987: Dallas Green, 53, Resigns as Cubs President, GM
item.description: Dallas Green, only three years after his recognition as MLB Executive of the Year, resigns as president and general manager of the Chicago Cubs over "philosophical differences" with the team's owners, the Tribune Company. Since taking the job six years ago, Green, 53, took the Cubs from last place to their first postseason appearance in 39 years as 1984 NL East champions. Photo: Flickr user pvsbond (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 1986: Orioles Trade Storm Davis to Padres for Williamson, Kennedy
item.description: The Baltimore Orioles trade 24-year-old right-handed starter Storm Davis to the San Diego Padres for reliever Mark Williamson and catcher Terry Kennedy. Photo: Baltimore Orioles (Public domain).

item.title: 1984: Jim Davenport, 51, Named Giants Manager for 1985
item.description: Former stalwart third baseman Jim Davenport, who on April 15, 1958 became the first man to officially bat for the relocated San Francisco Giants, is named the club's manager for 1985. Davenport, 51, is in the midst of a 60+ year pro baseball career that will include 51 years in the Giants' organization as a player, coach, MLB and minor-league manager, scout, and front office official.

item.title: 1983: Red Sox Farmhands Survive Capsizing, One Drowns off Florida
item.description: Boston Red Sox farmhands John Mitchell, Anthony Latham and Scott Skripko are deep-sea fishing off the Gulf Coast of Florida when their boat capsizes. Boat owner Mark Zastrowmy and Latham drown. Skripko and Mitchell survive over 20 hours in the water by clinging to debris; Skripko holds onto a cooler for 20 hours and Mitchell a bucket for 22 hours. Photo: CandL and Colorcraft (Public domain).

item.title: 1975: Montefusco Wins NL Rookie of the Year Award
item.description: John Montefusco, the San Francisco Giants' right-hander, wins the 1975 National League Rookie of the Year Award. Fred Lynn, the Boston Red Sox center-fielder, had won American League rookie honors two days before.

item.title: 1967: White Sox to Play Nine Night Games at Milwaukee in 1968
item.description: The Chicago White Sox, who drew only 985,634 fans to Comiskey Park despite a season of pennant contention in 1967, announce they will play nine night games, one against each American League foe, at Milwaukee County Stadium in 1968. Photo: Jwhouk (Public domain).

item.title: 1964: Stanka Named Pacific League MVP, Leads Nankai Hawks
item.description: Joe Stanka is named MVP of the Pacific League of Nippon Professional baseball after leading the Nankai Hawks over the Yomiuri Giants in the 1964 Japan Series.

item.title: 1963: Koufax Wins NL MVP, Edges Groat With 237 Points
item.description: Capping a brilliant 1963 season and a sweep of major awards during the month of October, Sandy Koufax breezes to the National League's Most Valuable Player Award. Today, he captures 14 of a possible 20 first place votes and 237 points to best Dick Groat of the St. Louis Cardinals (four, 190). Photo: publicity still (Public domain).

item.title: 1956: Dodgers Sell Ebbets Field to Marvin Kratter for $3 Million
item.description: The Brooklyn Dodgers sell Ebbets Field, their home since 1913, to real-estate developer Marvin Kratter for a price later revealed to be $3 million. The Dodgers will lease the ballpark from Kratter in 1957, with options to return for the next two seasons, but The New York Times warns that "the demise of Ebbets Field" has come "a step nearer reality." Photo: Wikimedia Commons (Public domain).

item.title: 1952: Cardinals Release Harry Brecheen, Browns Name Him Coach
item.description: The St. Louis Cardinals release longtime star left-hander Harry Brecheen, a two-time NL All-Star and hero of the 1946 World Series. Brecheen is immediately named a playing pitching coach by the American League St. Louis Browns. Photo: Press Association (Public domain).

item.title: 1884: Columbus Sells Players to Pittsburgh for $6,000, Disbands
item.description: The Columbus Buckeyes of the American Association sell their players to the Pittsburgh Alleghenys for $6,000 and disband the team. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1875: Boston Beats Hartford 7-4, Final Game of NA History
item.description: Boston defeats Hartford 7–4 in what proves to be the final game in the history of the NA. The Bostons claim the last 4 pennants in increasingly dominating fashion after the Athletics win the inaugural flag in 1871. Photo: Prescott & White (Public domain).

item.title: 1871: Athletics Beat Chicago 4-1, Clinch First Pro Championship
item.description: The Athletics of Philadelphia defeat the Chicago White Stockings in Brooklyn 4–1 to clinch the first professional baseball championship. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).
